title: The challenge and a recording as photograph
summary: What keeps him going; a recording loses time.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: The challenge is what we're after all the time; not the competition but the challenge of doing something, so that each time we come to it we can bring more than is really asked of us. And if somehow we can drag it out of ourselves, we feel a lot better for it and it's that good feeling that we're after.

It's a curious sense of accomplishment when you know something is happening and it doesn't make much difference if too many people aren't aware of it. The important thing is to do it, to experience it.
I have a suspicion that's what keeps us following this will of the wist; we know why, but it doesn't always make itself plain in the sort of environment in

which we live, because the rewards are not readily apparent. They lie mostly in hope, because once it's done it's passed because it's just a momentary thing. It lasts as long as the situation lasts and then it's gone and then it becomes a memory.
Aren't you lucky enough to record it?

But a recording is like a photograph. It loses the element of time. It's okay as a reference but it isn't a living force. It's people inter-reacting because of a lot of circumstances. It has to be at three o'clock in the afternoon on a Tuesday of February, and it can't really happen any other time When people talk about classical music always being the same, that's nonsense. It isn't, because the critical thing is at three o'clock in the afternoon of February 23; that's what's important.
